newsitem.title: JAPAN: Israel minister shrugs off Arab boycott call.
newsitem.headline: Israel minister shrugs off Arab boycott call.

text.p: Israel trade minister Natan Sharansky on Monday shrugged off an Arab call for a renewed economic boycott against the Jewish state, saying it was only symbolic and would have little economic impact.
"They (Arab countries) did not try to set up a proper boycott," Sharansky told Reuters in an interview in Tokyo. "It's all symbolic."
He said if Arab states had been serious about a boycott they would have included countries like Japan, the United States, France and England.
"They did not do it," Sharansky said.
Arab foreign ministers, angry at the building of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, last week urged an end to normal relations with Israel and a restoration of of economic sanctions.

The call by the Arab league followed daily clashes between Palestinians and Israeli troops as the Israeli-Palestinian peace process stalled over building of a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Sharansky, who returns to Jerusalem on Tuesday after a three-day visit to Japan, said the peace process as well as its effects on economic cooperation with the world, including the Arab world, were irreversible.

Japanese industrialists say an increasing number of companies, particularly high-tech firms, were interested in working with Israel after shunning the country for decades for fear of losing Arab markets and oil supplies.

Japanese official statistics show that while Japan's direct investment in Israel remains low, Tokyo has emerged as Israel's second largest export partner after the United States with diamonds and machinery at the top of Tokyo's shopping list.

Sharansky confirmed Israel would send representatives to Malta next week when ministers from the EU and the south Mediterranean, including Egypt, Syria, Lebanon, Jordan, Morocco, Tunisia, Algeria, and the Palestinian Authority will discuss possible areas for economic cooperation.
"We are not boycotting any meeting," he said.
